primary_meaning: A solemn, binding relationship and promised commitment initiated by God with His people, symbolizing divine grace, faithfulness, and the structural framework of God's redemptive plan for humanity, ultimately fulfilled in the New Covenant through Jesus Christ.

alternatives.meaning: A legal, conditional suzerain-vassal treaty emphasizing divine law, human obedience, and consequent material or spiritual blessings and curses.
An overarching theological framework dividing all of redemptive history into the Covenant of Works (pre-fall) and the Covenant of Grace (post-fall), as emphasized in Reformed Covenant Theology.
A marital union symbolizing the intimate, exclusive, and faithful love relationship between God and His people, or Christ and the Church.
A series of distinct, primarily unconditional, literal promises made specifically to national Israel that remain separate from God's program for the Church, as emphasized in Dispensationalism.

notes: While the fundamental definition of a covenant as a divinely initiated, binding relational promise has broad consensus, there are profound systemic disagreements in Christian theology regarding how these covenants relate to one another and structure biblical history (e.g., Covenant Theology vs. New Covenant Theology vs. Dispensationalism).
